newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Arbed says steel price pick-up confirmed.
newsitem.headline: Arbed says steel price pick-up confirmed.

text.p: Luxembourg-based steel group Arbed said on Wednesday that the first quarter of 1997 had confirmed the up-turn in steel sales prices which began towards the end of 1996 after a sharp fall.
Arbed, which announced it had fallen into loss in 1996, said in a statement that because of a shrinking economy European steel production had fallen in 1996.
At the same time clients' destocking and a sharp drop in spending on investments had contributed to the tumble in steel prices last year.
"It was not until the last months of 1996 that the trend turned around under the influence of a pick-up in demand accompanied by a selective increase in prices," Arbed said.
"This tendency has been confirmed in the first quarter of 1997," it added.
Arbed made a group loss of 1.21 billion Luxembourg francs after a 3.66 group net profit in 1995. It announced a 1996 consolidated net loss of 928 million francs versus a 6.615 billion profit.
Turnover fell 9.7 percent -- or 4.6 percent on a comparable consolidation basis -- to 232.23 billion francs.
Arbed said that in a "globally unfavourable" environment in 1996, it had reinforced its position on steel markets and pursued ongoing restructuring.
